problems.title: Add repeating decimals exactly
problems.question: Evaluate0.(27)+0.5(45).
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
steps: Their sum is 9/11.

problems.title: A negative factor stays outside a square root
problems.question: Put the factorx inside the radical in x√(−x).
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Domain x≤0, so x=−|x|. For nonnegativeu, v,√u√v=√(uv).

problems.title: Count divisors of a radical equation’s root
problems.question: How many positive divisors has the root of √(5x−1)=7?
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Squaring gives 5x−1=49, so x=10.
steps: Its divisors are 1,2,5,10, four in all.

problems.title: Similarity between an altitude-foot triangle and the original
problems.question: In acute ABC, AK and BD are altitudes, AC=b, BC=a, AB=c, and KC=m. FindKD.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: AnglesAKB=ADB=90°, so A, K, B, D are cyclic. The altitude-foot triangle CKD is similar to CAB.
steps: The corresponding ratio gives KD/AB=CK/CA=m/b. HenceKD=mc/b.

problems.title: A chord parallel to an isosceles base
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has sides 18,18,12 and an incircle. Find the distance between its contact points on the equal legs.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Semiperimeter=24. Each tangent segment from the apex is 24−12=12.
steps: The contact-point chord joins points at the same fraction12/18=2/3 along both legs. By similarity, it is 2/3 of the base12.
Its length is 8.

problems.title: Verify six radical identities
problems.question: How many printed radical equalities hold for every input in their common domains?
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Rationalise denominators using conjugates;√(a⁴)=a², and 2a/√a=2√a for a>0.
steps: The first, second, fourth, fifth, sixth identities are true.
Thus five are true on their stated common domains.

problems.title: Square roots of squares are absolute values
problems.question: Evaluate√(x²−2x+1)+√(x²−12x+36) at x=1.99.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The expression is|x−1|+|x−6|.

problems.title: Rationalise before ordering
problems.question: Ordera=7+3√3, b=1/(7−4√3), c=7+2√5, d=1/(5−2√6).
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The conjugate products are 1, so b=7+4√3, d=5+2√6.
steps: Their approximate values are d≈9.899, c≈11.472, a≈12.196, b≈13.928.
Thus the increasing order is d, c, a, b.

problems.title: Intersecting chords
problems.question: ChordsAB, CD meet at O, AO=4, BO=7, CO=2. FindCD.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: $AO\cdot BO=CO\cdot DO$.
steps: ThusDO=28/2=14. SinceO is inside CD, the full length is CO+DO=2+14=16.

problems.title: Three equal pieces of a trapezoid midline
problems.question: The diagonals divide a trapezoid’s midline into three equal pieces. Find the base ratio.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: For basesa≤b, the pieces have lengths a/2,(b−a)/2, a/2.
steps: Equality givesb−a=a, or b=2a.

problems.title: Count integers in two radical domains
problems.question: How many integers satisfy√(4x−1)>−3 and √(3x−1)<5?
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The first inequality is automatic onx≥1/4. The second requiresx≥1/3 and 3x−1<25.
steps: Together,1/3≤x<26/3. The integers are 1 through8, eight values.

problems.title: A vanishing radical factor
problems.question: Evaluate(√63−√21+√35)(√12−√27−√48+√75).
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The second factor is(2−3−4+5)√3=0.
steps: Multiplying any finite first factor by 0 gives 0.

problems.title: Exclude denominator zeros from numerator candidates
problems.question: Find the root sum of(2x−5)(x−3)√(2x+1)/(4x²−1)=0.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Domainx≥−1/2, butx≠±1/2. Numerator zeros are 5/2,3,−1/2.
steps: The radical zero−1/2 is excluded by the denominator. The valid roots are 5/2 and 3.
Their sum is 11/2=5.5.

problems.title: Check whether the geometry exists
problems.question: A line through B does not cross AC. Perpendicular distances from A, C to it are 8,16. M is midpoint AC and MD=10, where D is A’s foot. Find distance from M to C’s foot K.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: A, C lie on the same side of the line, so M has perpendicular distance(8+16)/2=12.
steps: Every distance from M to a point on that line must be at least12. But D lies on the line and MD is stated as10.
Thus no real configuration satisfies all the printed data. If the impossible value were ignored, the midpoint coordinates would formally give MD=MK.
problems.answer: No such configuration; the printed distances are inconsistent.
problems.note: The condition that the line does not cross AC makes the midpoint 12 from it, contradicting MD=10. A formal equal-distance calculation would suggest10, but that figure cannot exist.

problems.title: Power of a point through a cyclic quadrilateral
problems.question: ABC has A=80°, B=50°, AB=14. M∈AC, AM:MC=3:4, N∈AB, and CMNB is cyclic. FindAN.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: C=50°, so AC=AB=14 and AM=6. Power from A gives AM·AC=AN·AB.
steps: SinceAC=AB≠0, the equality reduces to AN=AM=6.

problems.title: A sum of squares forces three zeros
problems.question: Given|a+b|²+|b+c|²+|a+c|²=|a+b+c|², which listed relation follows?
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Expand the real squares and cancel cross terms to geta²+b²+c²=0.
steps: Every square is nonnegative, so a=b=c=0.
Among the printed options, a+b=2(b+c) then reads0=0 and is true.

problems.title: A linear inequality valid for every real input
problems.question: For whicha is ax≥a²−4+2x true for all realx?
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Rearrange to(a−2)x≥a²−4. A nonzero coefficient ofx cannot give a lower bound for every realx.
steps: Thusa=2 is necessary. It yields0≥0, so it is sufficient.

problems.title: An empty intersection of two half-lines
problems.question: Which listeda makes3x−7≤x+4 and 5(x+3)−2(x−1)<7x+a have no common solutions?
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The bounds are x≤11/2 and x>(17−a)/4.
steps: The intersection is empty exactly when(17−a)/4≥11/2, or a≤−5.
Only −5 is listed.

problems.title: A circle centre on a right triangle’s hypotenuse
problems.question: A right triangle has shorter leg6, hypotenuse10. A circle touches the longer leg, passes through the opposite acute vertex, and has centre on the hypotenuse. Find radius.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The other leg is 8. Put the right vertex at(0,0), short-leg endpoint A=(6,0), other endpoint B=(0,8). A centre O=(r,8−4r/3) has radiusr.
steps: Passing through A gives(r−6)²+(8−4r/3)²=r². This simplifies to 4r²−75r+225=0.
The roots are 15 and 15/4. A centre on the hypotenuse segment has 0≤r≤6, so only 15/4 is valid.

problems.title: A second median question with unmatched choices
problems.question: InDEF, DK is a median, KDE=70°, DKF=140°. FindDFE.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
steps: The equal lengths give D=(−1/2, tan40°/2), as follows by writing D=t(cos140°, sin140°) and imposing DE=DK.
ThereforeDFE=arctan(tan40°/3)≈15.6263°.
problems.answer: Approximately15.6263°; none of the listed choices.
problems.note: The stated median and angles do not give any of 20°,30°,45°,60°,70°,80°.

problems.title: Equal fourth powers of distinct real numbers
problems.question: Givena=b+1 anda⁴=b⁴, finda/b+b/a.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Real equal fourth powers implya=b ora=−b. The first contradictsa=b+1.
steps: Thusa=−b and −b=b+1, givinga=1/2, b=−1/2. Each quotient is −1, so their sum is −2.

problems.title: The midpoint of two fixed inputs
problems.question: The solutions of|x+2023|<|x−a| are exactly(−∞,1). Finda.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: This compares distances to −2023 and a. Its boundary is their midpoint(a−2023)/2.
steps: Set the midpoint to 1, so a=2025. Since2025>−2023, the points nearer−2023 do indeed lie to the left of 1.

problems.title: Horizontal width of a triangular feasible region
problems.question: A and B satisfy y≥−x+6, y≤−2x+14, y≤x+2. Maximise|x₂−x₁|.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: The lower bound must not exceed either upper bound:−x+6≤x+2 and −x+6≤−2x+14.
steps: These give2≤x≤8. Both extreme points are feasible:(2,4) and(8,−2).
Thus the greatest horizontal separation is 8−2=6.

problems.title: Projection onto a rhombus median line
problems.question: In rhombus ABCD, B=40°, M is midpoint BC, and N is A’s perpendicular foot on DM. FindCNM.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Scale sides to 1, writec=cos40°, s=sin40°. UseB=(0,0), A=(1,0), C=(c, s), M=(c/2, s/2), D=(1+c, s).
steps: Letw=D−M. Orthogonal projection gives N=M+tw, where t=[(A−M)·w]/|w|²=3/(5+4c).
Withp=C−N, q=M−N, the cosine formula(p·q)/(|p||q|) simplifies to √((1−c)/2)=sin20°.
Thuscos(CNM)=cos70°, so the interior angle is 70°.

problems.title: Carry an inscribed angle to a second circle
problems.question: ABC is inscribed with AB=AC, A=20°. D lies on minorarc AB; E lies beyond D on AD and on A’s side of BC. CircleBDE meets AB again at F. FindEFB.
problems.idea: Keep domains and geometric feasibility in view while simplifying.
formulas: Base angles B=C=80°. SinceD lies on minorarc AB, angle ADB=180°−ACB=100°.
steps: DA and DE are opposite rays, so EDB=80°.
In the stated ordering, D and F subtend chord EB from the same side in circle BDE. ThereforeEFB=EDB=80°.
